Maria: Heads-up — ran the day-0 TTL bucketed eviction experiment on staging after the kernel selection change. Seeing unexpected drop in prompt cache hit rate and a spiky GPU OOM on node gpu-prod-12. Dumping summary below, need quick triage.

Tom: what changed in kernel selection? we just added fused-attn path for seq_len<=128 right?

Maria: yep. compiled with new fused kernels that prioritize throughput for short sequences. Perf numbers:
- baseline (old kernels): kv_hit_rate=0.62, avg_latency=78ms, tokens/sec=4200
- new-kernel: kv_hit_rate=0.47, avg_latency=72ms, tokens/sec=4600
- but GPU memory pressure increased: p99 memory=12.6GB -> 14.8GB on same batch mix

Li: lower hit rate but higher tokens/sec suggests we're mis-keying or warmup got worse. Did the cache key normalization change?

Maria: no explicit key change. But kernel changes altered how we shard batched requests (we now split short requests differently). Hypothesis: batching heuristics cause different prefix alignments -> worse cache reuse + more KV copies to GPU.

Aisha: can you paste the sampling profiler output? small snippet is fine.

Maria: pasted sample from perf-probe (top lines):
```
kv.copy_bytes/sec  ->  2.4GB/s (old) -> 3.7GB/s (new)
kv.lookup_latency   ->  3.1ms -> 4.9ms
kernel.exec_time    ->  18ms -> 15ms (per-call)
cache.hitrate       ->  0.62 -> 0.47
evict.avg_batch     ->  128 -> 96
```

Ben: that copy_bytes jump explains OOM. If more KV shards are being copied per request we blow up mem. Might be from per-request padding differences when using fused kernels.

Tom: can we toggle the batching fallback so short-seq keep old sharding? quick A/B?

Maria: I pushed a toggle flag in staging, flag name `runtime.experimental.shortseq_shard_v2=false`. Will run 1h test.

DeployBot: Deploy 1903456795 by maria to staging succeeded :white_check_mark:

Li: also see fragmentation metric spike — the allocator shows many small allocations around 32KB-256KB after the change. That suggests more ephemeral KV buffers.

Aisha: two prongs: 1) mitigate by coalescing KV copies (aggregate per-batch) 2) tune TTL buckets to be coarser so eviction churn is lower during warmup. Thoughts?

Ben: agree. For (2) maybe expand bucket width for short-lived prefix keys from 30s->90s for warmup ramp. That reduces churn while hit-rate stabilizes.

Maria: tried a quick config: `kv.eviction.buckets = [30,60,120,300] -> [90,180,360,600]` on a node. Early sign: hit_rate rose to 0.55, memory pressure fell ~600MB, but avg latency +2ms.

Tom: +2ms acceptable for staging. Need to quantify at scale. Also want to instrument `cache_key_digest` distribution to confirm key collisions or per-prefix variance.

Aisha: we should also capture sequence length in key fingerprint (currently it is omitted to maximize reuse). If fused kernel's padding strategy changes reuse semantics, adding seq_len might actually help by preventing wrong-sharing. But could reduce cross-seq reuse. We need an experiment.

Maria: created branch `rekey/seq-len-opt` with opt-in flag. Experiment plan: 4 nodes, matrix: {shortseq_shard_v2 on/off} x {seqlen_in_key on/off} x {bucket_coarse on/off}. Run 2h each.

Li: how will we measure? primary metrics: kv_hit_rate, evict_cycles/sec, gpu_mem_peak, request_p99. Secondary: tokens/sec, kernel_exec_time.

Ben: one more note — our LRU decay window may be too aggressive. After kernel change we see more temporary transient keys that should be aged slower. Adjustable param `lru.decay_tau` can be increased from 60s->180s for warmup. That plus coarse buckets might reduce churn without rekeying.

Tom: can we run a synthetic test that reproduces the padding/batching pattern? If we can make deterministic batches we can isolate whether it's sharding or keying.

Maria: yes, I'm creating a replay script that sends short sequences with similar arrival patterns. Will share results in this thread when done.

DeployBot: CI pipeline: perf-tests/replay-shortseq completed (job 1903456810) with artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/staging/1903456810/logs

Aisha: quick interim mitigation for prod: enable chunked-KV-copy (coalesce copies) and increase GPU eviction threshold by 5% so eviction doesn't thrash during bursts. We'll run for 24h and watch.

Maria: rolled mitigation to prod-canary1 at 1903456842. Observed: gpu-usage down 8%, hit_rate regained to 0.59 on canary, no OOMs.

Li: good. For root cause, my bet is interplay: fused kernel changed internal padding + our batching policy changed shard boundaries -> more unique physical keys on GPU -> more copies and fragmentation -> eviction thrash.

Ben: follow-ups:
- Maria: run matrix experiments, share CSV w/metrics
- Tom: add deterministic replay harness to perf repo
- Li: add allocator heatmap and key digest histogram to perf dashboard
- Aisha: keep prod mitigation on and prepare rollout plan if stable

Maria: noted. I'll post a short postmortem and a proposed config PR that sets warmup presets when kernel toggles flip.

Tom: thumbs up. If we can auto-detect hit-rate regression on deploy and flip warmup presets automatically, that would save manual ops.

Aisha: opening an eval alert: `perf.regression.kv_hit_rate` to fire when delta<-0.05 within 30m of deploy.

Maria: thanks all. will update with experiment CSVs and replay artifacts. :coffee:
